Lines the given layers up on an edge or a centre line.

Takes explicit ids rather than acting on a selection: what an agent
asked for should be legible in the journal afterwards.

Adds a named style bundle to the document, or replaces one by name.

Layers that were styled by it keep their properties: applying a preset
sets properties, it does not create a link, so deleting one cannot

Declares a named opening in the document, making it a template.

Refused at definition time — not merely reported by validation — for a
name already taken, a layer that is not there, a kind that does not
match the layer, or **a layer that is protected or read-only**.

That last refusal is why this is an operation rather than a hand edit.
Filling a slot is already refused on protected chrome, because a fill
is an `Update`. Defining one is not a fill, and without this check a
template could advertise an opening that always fails: the author would
think they had offered something, and every variant would refuse.

Changes an existing slot, by name.

The same checks a definition faces, because the result has to be a slot
that could have been defined.

slot.description: The slot's new content. Its `name` may differ, which renames it.

oneOf.description: Removes a named opening. The layer it pointed at is untouched.

Applies a named style bundle to a layer.

Compiles to the [`Update`](Operation::Update) the preset describes
before anything is changed, which is what makes applying a preset and
setting the same properties by hand the same picture — and what makes
a protected layer refuse here without a preset-specific check.

Color.description:
An sRGB colour, `#rrggbb` or `#rrggbbaa`.

Stored as written so a document round-trips exactly; validation checks the

Transform.description: Position, size, and rotation of a layer in its parent's coordinate space.

width.description: Box width; must be finite and not negative.

height.description: Box height; must be finite and not negative.

rotation.description: Clockwise rotation in degrees about the box centre.

TextAlign.description: Horizontal text alignment inside the layer box.

oneOf.description: Aligned to the left edge.
Centred horizontally.
Aligned to the right edge.

FontStyle.description: Whether glyphs stand upright or slant.

oneOf.description: The upright face.

The italic face (an oblique stands in when the family has no true
italic — the font set still keys it as italic).

width.description:
Width in document units; must be finite and 0 or more.

**Painted inset** on a rect and an ellipse (D5): the stroke grows
inward from the transform box, so the box is the visual box and
nothing that reasons about layout has to know whether a shape is
stroked. A line has no interior, so its stroke is centred on the
segment instead — half of it falls either side of the box's middle.

One caveat, measured rather than assumed: a width below one device
pixel is drawn as a *hairline* centred on the geometric edge, and a
hairline occupies a whole pixel row. A 0.5-wide stroke therefore
spills up to half a pixel outside the box on each side. It is
deterministic and identical on every target, so it is documented here
rather than refused — but at that width the box is not quite the
visual box.

VerticalAlign.description: Where the text block sits vertically in the layer box.

oneOf.description:
The first baseline one ascent below the box top — the behaviour every
build up to 1.6 had, and the default so nothing moves.
The block centred in the box's height.
The block's last line resting on the box bottom.

ImageFit.description: How an image is scaled into its box.

oneOf.description: Stretch to the box, ignoring aspect ratio.
Scale down to fit inside the box, keeping aspect ratio.
Scale to cover the box, keeping aspect ratio, cropping the overflow.

ShapeKind.description: The geometry of a [`ShapeLayer`], tagged by `"kind"` in JSON.

anyOf.description: A rectangle filling the transform box.

cornerRadius.description:
Corner radius in document units; 0 is a square corner.

Clamped to half the shorter side when it is drawn, so a radius
larger than the box makes a stadium rather than a refusal.

anyOf.description: An ellipse inscribed in the transform box.

A straight segment across the middle of the transform box, from the
left edge to the right.

The box *is* the line: `width` is its length, `rotation` is its angle,
and `height` is layout only — nothing is drawn above or below the
middle. A second endpoint in the payload would be a second way of
saying where a layer is, and `move`, `resize` and `rotate` would then
have to mean something different for this layer kind than for the
other four (maintainer's decision, 2026-09-09).

A geometry this build does not know, preserved as written and refused
when something tries to change or draw it — the same bargain as
[`Effect::Other`] and [`BlendMode::Other`] (D21).

CreateLayer.description: Add a layer to the document.

transform.description: Its box in the parent's coordinate space.

oneOf.description: A text layer.

text.description: The text; `\n` starts a new line.

fontFamily.description: Font family, resolved at render time against the caller's fonts.

color.description:
Fill colour, or none for hollow (stroke-only) text. Absent means
the pre-1.7 default of black, as it always did.

lineHeight.description: Line height as a multiple of the font size.

fontWeight.description: Font weight, 100–900; 400 is the regular face.

letterSpacing.description: Extra space between characters, in pixels.

verticalAlign.description: Where the block sits vertically in the box.

oneOf.description: An image layer referencing an asset already in the document.
An empty group.
A vector graphic layer referencing an imported SVG asset.

A rectangle, an ellipse or a line, drawn from the document.

No implicit default paint: a caller that sends neither `fill` nor
`stroke` gets an invisible shape, because guessing black here would
make "no fill" impossible to ask for. The surfaces people actually
type at — the CLI, the MCP tools, the interface — apply their own
defaults on top of this.

shape.description:
The geometry. A kind this build does not draw is refused here
rather than stored: creating a layer nothing can render is not a
document a newer build wrote, it is a mistake being made now.

BlendMode.description:
How a layer composites onto what is beneath it.

The whole CSS separable-and-non-separable set, every one of which was
checked to rasterize before it was named here — a mode that only
round-trips would be a promise the pixels do not keep.

[`BlendMode::Other`] is what a mode written by some newer build becomes:
preserved verbatim, because losing it would mean a document came back
damaged, but **refused at render time** rather than quietly composited as
`normal`. Silently drawing the wrong thing is the worse failure: it looks
like it worked.

anyOf.description: Plain source-over compositing.
Darkens: multiplies the two colours.
Lightens: the inverse of multiplying the inverses.
Multiplies or screens, depending on the backdrop.
Keeps the darker of the two.
Keeps the lighter of the two.
Brightens the backdrop to reflect the source.
Darkens the backdrop to reflect the source.
`Overlay` with the layers swapped.
A softer `HardLight`.
The absolute difference of the two.
Like `Difference`, with less contrast.
The source's hue, the backdrop's saturation and luminosity.
The source's saturation, the backdrop's hue and luminosity.
The source's hue and saturation, the backdrop's luminosity.
The source's luminosity, the backdrop's hue and saturation.

A mode this build does not render, preserved as written and refused
when something tries to draw it.

Effect.description:
One adjustment in a layer's effect stack.

Tagged by `type`, so the JSON reads as what it is. [`Effect::Other`] keeps
an effect written by a newer build verbatim and refuses to render it —
the same bargain as [`BlendMode::Other`]: never lose it, never guess at it.

The amounts are multipliers where 1 means "unchanged", which is what
`filter: brightness(1.2)` means everywhere else, so a number copied from a
CSS example does what it looks like it does.

anyOf.description: Scales each channel. 1 is unchanged, 0 is black.
Pushes each channel away from mid grey. 1 is unchanged, 0 is flat grey.
Scales colourfulness. 1 is unchanged, 0 is greyscale.
A Gaussian blur.

radius.description: Standard deviation, in document units. 0 does nothing.

anyOf.description:
Seeded monochrome noise, multiplied over the layer.

The seed is part of the document, not the run: the same document
produces the same grain on every machine and in every render (NFR-3).
Grain from a clock or a random number generator would quietly break
the one property this project is built on.

amount.description: How far the noise swings either side of unchanged, 0 to 1.

scale.description: Size of the noise features; 1 is fine grain, larger is coarser.

anyOf.description:
A soft offset copy of the layer's alpha, drawn beneath it.

A glow is this with `dx` and `dy` at 0, and Lift is this with a small
offset and a soft blur. There is no second primitive for either: a
centred shadow *is* a glow, and two names for one filter would be two
things to keep bit-identical for no gain.

dx.description:
Horizontal offset in document units.

A fractional offset is resampled by the filter and reads slightly
softer; whole numbers give the crispest edge.

dy.description: Vertical offset in document units. See `dx`.

blur.description:
Standard deviation of the blur, 0 or more. 0 is a hard-edged
offset copy.

color.description:
Shadow colour. An `#rrggbbaa` alpha becomes the flood opacity, so
a shadow's strength is written where every other colour writes it.

anyOf.description:
An effect this build does not know, preserved as written and refused
when something tries to draw it.

UpdateLayer.description:
Change properties of an existing layer.

Every field is optional and means "leave alone" when absent. `name` is
doubly optional: `Some(None)` clears the name, `None` leaves it.

name.description: New name, or `Some(None)` to remove it.

blendMode.description:
How the layer composites onto what is beneath it.

A mode this build does not render is refused here, so a value that
would fail at render time cannot get into a document through this
build in the first place.

effects.description:
Replace the whole effect stack.

The whole stack rather than one effect at a time: order is part of the
meaning — a blurred thing desaturated is not a desaturated thing
blurred — and an insert-at-index operation would be a second, subtler
way of saying what this already says. Undo restores the previous stack
like any other property.

color.description:
Text layers: new colour. Absent leaves it, `null` clears it.

Doubly optional like `name` and the shape `fill`, and for the same
reason: "no fill" is a real value text can have — a stroke-only layer
is the hollow style — so there has to be a way to say it that is not
"leave it alone".

letterSpacing.description: Text layers: new letter spacing, in pixels.

asset.description:
Image and SVG layers: draw a different asset.

The asset must already be in the document — importing is not an
operation (it copies a file, which is not reversible), so swapping to
something that was never imported is refused rather than half-done.

fill.description:
Shape layers: new interior paint. Absent leaves it, `null` clears it.

Doubly optional like `name` and the canvas background, and for the
same reason: "no fill" is a real value a shape can have, so there has
to be a way to say it that is not "leave it alone".

stroke.description:
Shape and text layers: the whole stroke. Absent leaves it, `null`
clears it.

The whole stroke rather than colour and width separately: a width
without a colour is not a stroke, and letting one be set alone would
mean inventing a colour nobody asked for. On a text layer the stroke
is painted centred on the glyph outline, fill first, so it never eats
the letter.

cornerRadius.description:
Shape layers whose geometry is a rect: new corner radius.

Not nullable: 0 is the square-cornered value, so there is nothing for
`null` to mean that 0 does not already say.

allowLocked.description:
Change the layer even though it is locked.

Needed to unlock a layer at all, and kept explicit so that no ordinary
edit slips past a lock by accident.

AlignEdge.description: Which edge or axis an alignment lines up.

oneOf.description: Left edges.
Right edges.
Top edges.
Bottom edges.
Horizontal centres.
Vertical centres.
Left to right.
Top to bottom.
Both at once.

SnapTarget.description: What a layer is snapped to.

oneOf.description: An edge of another layer.
An edge of the canvas.

Preset.description: A named bundle of style properties.

name.description: What it is called. Unique within a document.

description.description:
What it is for, for whoever is choosing between presets — including an
agent, which is the case that needs it most.

properties.description: The properties it sets. Anything left out is left alone on apply.

PresetProperties.description:
What a preset sets.

Every field optional, and absent means "leave alone" — so a preset that
only names a colour is a colour preset, and applying it does not quietly
reset a layer's font.

Deliberately no transform: a style is not a position. A preset that moved
layers would be a template, and templates already exist.

letterSpacing.description: Text layers: letter spacing, in pixels.

verticalAlign.description: Text layers: vertical alignment in the box.

effects.description: Any layer: the whole effect stack.

fill.description:
Shape layers: interior paint.

A plain `Option`, unlike the update's doubly-optional `fill`: a preset
that omits it leaves the fill alone, and there is no spelling that
clears one. A style says what a thing looks like; "looks like nothing"
is not a house style, and a preset that could silently empty a shape
would be a sharp edge on a feature whose whole point is repeatability.

stroke.description:
Shape layers: edge paint. See [`PresetProperties::fill`] for why it
cannot be cleared.

Slot.description: A named opening in a template.

name.description: What a caller names this slot by. Unique within a document.

kind.description: What may be supplied for it.

description.description:
What this slot is for, for whoever is filling it — including an agent,
which is the case that needs it most.

required.description: Whether a variant must supply it.

SlotKind.description: What a slot lets a caller supply.

oneOf.description: The text of a text layer.
The asset an image layer draws.

The fill colour of a text layer, or of a shape layer.

One slot kind for both, resolved by the layer it points at (D8): a
text layer's `color` and a shape layer's `fill` are the same question
asked of two payloads, and a template that wanted a brand colour in
both a headline and the badge behind it should not need two slot
kinds to say so. A shape's *stroke* colour is not slot-able — a stroke
is a colour and a width together, and half of one is not a value.
